nodes.title: Ecosystem Concepts — Food Chains, Trophic Levels & Ecological Pyramids
prelimsNote: Ecosystem = biotic + abiotic components interacting as a unit (UPSC 2015); decomposers (bacteria, fungi) recycle nutrients (UPSC 2013).
10% law (Lindeman): only ~10% of energy passes to the next trophic level — food chains rarely exceed 4–5 links (UPSC 2013).
Pyramid of energy is always upright; pyramid of biomass is inverted in aquatic ecosystems (phytoplankton < zooplankton); pyramid of numbers inverted in a tree ecosystem.
Correct marine sequence: diatoms → crustaceans → herrings (UPSC 2014); detritivores include earthworms, dung beetles, woodlice (UPSC 2021).
Phytoplankton are the main primary producers of the oceans and a major carbon sink (UPSC 2012, 2021).

nodes.title: Biogeochemical Cycles — Carbon, Nitrogen, Water & Phosphorus
prelimsNote: Carbon is added to the atmosphere by respiration, volcanic action and decay of organic matter — photosynthesis removes it (UPSC 2014).
Nitrogen enters soil via lightning, nitrogen-fixing bacteria (Rhizobium in legumes), cyanobacteria like Nostoc (UPSC 2013).
Phosphorus cycle has no atmospheric phase — it is a sedimentary cycle (weathering of rocks); UPSC 2021.
Agricultural soils release nitrogen oxides and cattle release ammonia (UPSC 2019).
Sulphur cycle: SO₂ from fossil fuels returns as acid rain.

nodes.title: Ecologically Sensitive Areas — ESZ, Biodiversity Hotspots
prelimsNote: Hotspot criteria (Norman Myers/CI): at least 1,500 endemic vascular plants and ≥70% of original habitat lost (UPSC 2011).
India's 4 hotspots: Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats–Sri Lanka, Sundaland (Nicobar Islands).
Eco-Sensitive Zones are notified under the Environment (Protection) Act 1986 — not under the Wildlife Protection Act (UPSC 2014).
Gadgil (WGEEP, 2011) and Kasturirangan (HLWG, 2013) reports dealt with protecting the Western Ghats (UPSC 2016).
ESZs extend up to 10 km around protected areas (default guideline).

nodes.title: Biodiversity — Types, Importance & Threats
prelimsNote: Levels: genetic, species, ecosystem diversity; alpha (within community), beta (between communities), gamma (regional).
Diversity increases towards the equator and decreases with altitude (UPSC 2011).
Ecosystem services: provisioning, regulating, cultural, supporting (Millennium Ecosystem Assessment — UPSC 2012).
Himalayas lie at the meeting point of Palaearctic, Indo-Malayan and Ethiopian realms (UPSC 2011).
India: ~2.4% of world land area, ~7–8% of recorded species; one of 17 megadiverse countries.

nodes.title: Biodiversity Loss — Causes, IPBES Reports & India's Status
prelimsNote: Main drivers (HIPPO): habitat loss, invasive species, pollution, population, over-exploitation; climate change adds to them.
IPBES (2019) Global Assessment: about 1 million species threatened with extinction.
'Sixth mass extinction' refers to human-driven over-exploitation, habitat loss and climate change (UPSC 2018).
Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (CBD COP15, 2022): '30 by 30' — protect 30% of land and sea by 2030.

nodes.title: In-Situ Conservation — National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuaries, Tiger Reserves
prelimsNote: National parks: no grazing or human activity, no collection of forest produce; sanctuaries allow some activities (UPSC 2012).
Biosphere Reserves (UNESCO MAB): core, buffer and transition zones; best strategy to conserve biodiversity with traditional human life (UPSC 2014).
Project Tiger 1973; tiger reserves notified by States on NTCA's recommendation; Nagarjunasagar–Srisailam is the largest tiger reserve (critical tiger habitat area — UPSC 2020).
Project Elephant 1992; MIKE (Monitoring Illegal Killing of Elephants) under CITES; M-STrIPES is a tiger-reserve monitoring app (UPSC 2017).
Community and Conservation Reserves added by the WPA amendment of 2002.

nodes.title: Ex-Situ Conservation — Zoos, Gene Banks & Seed Vaults
prelimsNote: Ex-situ = outside natural habitat: botanical gardens (UPSC 2011), zoos, gene banks, seed banks, cryopreservation (−196 °C liquid nitrogen).
Svalbard Global Seed Vault (Norway) stores duplicate seed samples; ICAR-NBPGR (New Delhi) holds India's national gene bank.
Central Zoo Authority (WPA 1991 amendment) regulates zoos.
Captive breeding: Great Indian Bustard and Gharial programmes support recovery.

nodes.title: Man-Animal Conflict — Human-Wildlife Interface & Mitigation
prelimsNote: Elephants: herds led by the oldest female (matriarch); gestation up to ~22 months; Asian elephant is Endangered (UPSC 2020).
Conflict hotspots: elephant corridors, crop-raiding near PAs, leopard incursions in cities.
Mitigation: corridors, early-warning systems, compensation, bee-fences (Project RE-HAB).
A protected wild animal can be killed only if it becomes dangerous to human life after due process — mere apprehension is not sufficient ground (UPSC 2022).

nodes.title: Wildlife Crime — Poaching, Trade & CITES
prelimsNote: CITES (1975): Appendix I (trade banned), II (regulated), III (listed by one country); legally binding but does not replace national laws.
TRAFFIC is a wildlife-trade monitoring network of WWF and IUCN — not a UNEP bureau (UPSC 2017).
Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB) under WPA (2006 amendment) coordinates enforcement.
Red sanders (endemic to Andhra's Eastern Ghats) is heavily smuggled; listed as Endangered (UPSC 2016).

nodes.title: International Biodiversity Conventions — CBD, Ramsar, CITES
prelimsNote: CBD (Rio 1992): conservation, sustainable use, fair benefit sharing; Cartagena Protocol (biosafety), Nagoya Protocol (access & benefit sharing).
Ramsar (1971, Iran): parties designate wetlands of international importance; Montreux Record lists threatened sites — Keoladeo and Loktak (UPSC 2014).
CMS/Bonn Convention (migratory species) — India hosted CMS COP13 (Gandhinagar, 2020).
International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources (FAO) and CITES are other biodiversity treaties (UPSC 2014).

nodes.title: Wetlands — Conservation, Ramsar Sites & Threats
prelimsNote: India has 90+ Ramsar sites (as of 2025); Tamil Nadu has the most.
Wetlands act as the 'kidneys of the earth' because aquatic plants absorb heavy metals and excess nutrients (UPSC 2022).
Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules 2017 under EPA; Montreux Record: Keoladeo, Loktak (Chilika removed 2002).
Harike wetland lies at the Beas–Sutlej confluence — UPSC 2014 asked which wetlands sit at river confluences.

nodes.title: River Pollution — Ganga, Yamuna & Namami Gange Programme
prelimsNote: Namami Gange (2014) under the National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG, registered society).
National Ganga River Basin Authority (2009) treated the river basin as the unit of planning; it was chaired by the PM, not a CM (UPSC 2016).
Ganga declared the National River (2008); Ganges river dolphin is the National Aquatic Animal (UPSC 2015).
Threats to Ganges dolphins: dams, pollution, fishing nets, sand mining (UPSC 2014).

nodes.title: Ocean Resource Degradation & Marine Pollution
prelimsNote: Microbeads in personal-care products accumulate in oceans and harm marine life (UPSC 2019).
Coral bleaching from heat stress; ocean acidification dissolves carbonate shells.
Dead zones from nutrient run-off cause hypoxia; harmful algal blooms produce toxins (UPSC 2011).
Global Plastics Treaty negotiations (UNEA 2022 mandate) were still unresolved (as of 2025).

nodes.title: Air Pollution — Sources, Health Impact & Policy (BS Norms, NCAP)
prelimsNote: National AQI (2014): 8 pollutants — PM10, PM2.5, NO₂, SO₂, CO, O₃, NH₃, Pb (UPSC 2016).
WHO Air Quality Guidelines 2021: PM2.5 annual 5 µg/m³, 24-hour 15 µg/m³; PM2.5 (not PM10) enters the bloodstream; ozone triggers asthma (UPSC 2022).
Crop-residue burning releases CO, NOx, PM and SO₂ (UPSC 2019); benzene from vehicle exhaust, tobacco smoke, wood burning (UPSC 2020).
NCAP (2019): 40% PM reduction by 2025-26 in non-attainment cities; BS-VI norms from April 2020 (leapfrogged BS-V).
Photochemical smog: NOx + VOCs + sunlight → ozone, PAN; London smog: SO₂ + smoke + fog.

nodes.title: Water Pollution — Industrial, Agricultural & Municipal Sources
prelimsNote: BOD measures oxygen needed by microbes to decompose organic matter — high BOD means more pollution (UPSC 2017).
Eutrophication from nitrates/phosphates → algal blooms → hypoxia (UPSC 2011).
Drinking water contaminants: arsenic (Ganga–Brahmaputra plains), fluoride (fluorosis), nitrates (blue-baby syndrome) — UPSC 2013.
UV radiation disinfects water by killing microbes (UPSC 2012).

nodes.title: Soil Pollution — Pesticides, Heavy Metals & Remediation
prelimsNote: Carbofuran, methyl parathion, phorate and triazophos are pesticides viewed with concern (UPSC 2019).
Heavy-metal diseases: Minamata (mercury), Itai-itai (cadmium), arsenicosis (arsenic).
Bioremediation uses microbes/plants to clean pollutants — cheaper and on-site (UPSC 2017); Oilzapper (TERI) degrades oil sludge (UPSC 2011).
Neem-coated urea slows nitrogen release and limits leaching (UPSC 2016).

nodes.title: E-Waste — Management Rules, Health Impact & Extended Producer Responsibility
prelimsNote: E-waste contains lead, mercury, cadmium, beryllium and brominated flame retardants (UPSC 2013).
E-Waste (Management) Rules 2022 (in force 2023): EPR certificates traded via CPCB portal; producers bear collection responsibility (UPSC 2019).
R2 (Responsible Recycling) standard is for e-waste recycling practices (UPSC 2021).
India is the third-largest e-waste generator (after China and the USA).

nodes.title: Plastic Pollution — Single Use Plastic Ban & Circular Economy
prelimsNote: Identified single-use plastic items banned from 1 July 2022 (Plastic Waste Management Amendment Rules 2021).
Carry-bag thickness minimum 120 microns (from Dec 2022); EPR guidelines for plastic packaging (2022).
PET is recyclable into fibres and bottles; incineration emits GHGs (UPSC 2022).
Microbeads banned in rinse-off cosmetics by BIS (2020) (UPSC 2019).

nodes.title: Noise & Light Pollution
prelimsNote: Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules 2000 under EPA: day/night limits for industrial, commercial, residential and silence zones.
Silence zones: 100 m around hospitals, schools, courts.
Light pollution disrupts nocturnal species and bird migration; India's first dark-sky reserve at Hanle (Ladakh, 2022).
Never asked in UPSC Prelims so far — a likely gap area.

nodes.title: Oil Spills — Impact & International Conventions
prelimsNote: Oil forms a surface film blocking oxygen and light; harms seabirds and mammals.
Clean-up: booms, skimmers, dispersants, bioremediation (Oilzapper — UPSC 2011).
MARPOL (IMO, 1973/78) prevents ship pollution; India's National Oil Spill Disaster Contingency Plan coordinated by the Coast Guard.
Sand mining and coastal pollution damage marine ecosystems (UPSC 2018).

nodes.title: Climate Change — Scientific Basis, IPCC Reports & Evidence
prelimsNote: IPCC (1988, WMO + UNEP) assesses science; AR6 (2021–23) — human influence 'unequivocal'.
Warming beyond 2 °C threatens coral reefs, food production and sea level (UPSC 2014).
Carbon fertilization: higher CO₂ boosts plant photosynthesis (UPSC 2018).
Low clouds reflect sunlight (cooling); high thin clouds trap outgoing infrared (warming) — UPSC 2022 swapped these.
Methane hydrates under ocean floors/permafrost could release methane on warming (UPSC 2019).

nodes.title: Paris Agreement — NDCs, Finance & Implementation
prelimsNote: Adopted at COP21 (2015), in force 2016; goal: well below 2 °C, pursue 1.5 °C; NDCs updated every 5 years (UPSC 2016).
INDCs were submitted before Paris; they became NDCs on ratification (UPSC 2016).
Article 6: carbon markets — 6.2 bilateral, 6.4 UN-supervised mechanism (operationalised at COP29, 2024).
India's updated NDC (2022): 45% emissions-intensity cut by 2030 (vs 2005), 50% non-fossil power capacity, 2.5–3 billion t CO₂ sink; net zero by 2070 (Panchamrit at COP26).
NCQG (COP29, 2024): developed countries to mobilise at least US$300 billion a year by 2035.

nodes.title: International Solar Alliance — India's Leadership
prelimsNote: Launched by India and France at COP21 Paris (2015); HQ Gurugram — first intergovernmental body headquartered in India (UPSC 2016).
Membership opened to all UN members (2020 amendment) — but not ALL UN members are members (UPSC 2016 trap).
Initiatives: One Sun One World One Grid (OSOWOG), Green Grids Initiative with UK (COP26).
Aim: mobilise US$1 trillion solar investment by 2030.

nodes.title: Carbon Markets — Emissions Trading, Carbon Tax & Green Bonds
prelimsNote: Kyoto mechanisms: Emissions Trading, Clean Development Mechanism (CERs), Joint Implementation (UPSC 2011, 2016).
Carbon markets do NOT transfer resources from the private sector to the State — UPSC 2023 Statement-II was false.
India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme 2023 under the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act 2022; Bureau of Energy Efficiency administers it.
Social cost of carbon = economic damage from emitting one extra tonne of CO₂ (UPSC 2020); GHG Protocol is an accounting standard (UPSC 2016).
Sovereign Green Bonds issued by India from 2023.

nodes.title: Loss & Damage — Climate Finance for Developing Nations
prelimsNote: Loss & Damage Fund agreed at COP27 (Sharm el-Sheikh, 2022), operationalised at COP28 (Dubai, 2023); hosted by the World Bank initially.
Warsaw International Mechanism (2013) first addressed loss and damage.
Green Climate Fund (2010, HQ Songdo, South Korea) helps developing countries with mitigation and adaptation (UPSC 2015).
Global Environment Facility is a financial mechanism for CBD, UNFCCC, UNCCD, Stockholm and Minamata conventions (UPSC 2014).

nodes.title: Climate Change & Agriculture — Food Security Implications
prelimsNote: Rice paddies are the most important anthropogenic crop source of both methane and N₂O (UPSC 2022).
Climate-smart agriculture: GACSA (Global Alliance for Climate-Smart Agriculture, FAO-backed — UPSC 2018); climate-smart villages (CCAFS — UPSC 2021).
NICRA (ICAR, 2011) develops climate-resilient technologies.
SRI (alternate wetting and drying) reduces seed needs and methane emissions (UPSC 2022).

nodes.title: Climate Change & Urbanisation — Heat Islands & Flooding
prelimsNote: Urban heat island: cities warmer than surroundings due to concrete, low vegetation, waste heat.
Miyawaki method creates dense mini-forests in urban areas (UPSC 2022).
Heat Action Plans (Ahmedabad 2013, first in South Asia); NDMA heat-wave guidelines.
Sponge-city concepts and blue–green infrastructure reduce urban flooding.

nodes.title: Kigali Agreement — HFCs & Ozone Layer
prelimsNote: Montreal Protocol (1987) phases out ozone-depleting substances; universally ratified.
Kigali Amendment (2016): phase down HFCs, which are not ozone-depleting but are potent GHGs; India's baseline 2024–26, freeze 2028.
HFCs are used in refrigeration, aerosols, foam-blowing and fire suppression — UPSC 2023 asked how many of aerosols, foams, fire retardants and lubricants use them.
Polar stratospheric clouds enable ozone-hole chemistry over Antarctica (UPSC 2011); CFCs were used in aerosols, foams and refrigeration (UPSC 2012).

nodes.title: Arctic & Antarctic — Melting Ice, Sea Level Rise & Geopolitics
prelimsNote: Arctic Council members: Canada, Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Russia, Sweden, USA — India is an observer (2013) (UPSC 2014).
India's Arctic station Himadri (Svalbard, 2008); Antarctic stations Maitri and Bharati; Antarctic Act 2022.
Polar Code (IMO): safety code for ships in polar waters (UPSC 2022).
India's Arctic Policy (2022): six pillars; Arctic warming nearly four times the global average.

nodes.title: Desertification & Land Degradation — LDN Targets
prelimsNote: UNCCD (1994) is the only legally binding agreement linking environment and development to land management (UPSC 2016).
India hosted UNCCD COP14 (2019); target to restore 26 million ha of degraded land by 2030.
ISRO's Desertification Atlas: nearly 30% of India's land degraded.
Prosopis juliflora (invasive) spreads in degraded arid lands (UPSC 2018).

nodes.title: Groundwater Depletion — Causes, Regional Hotspots & Policy
prelimsNote: India is the largest groundwater user — about a quarter of global extraction (UN World Water Development Report 2022; UPSC 2023).
Central Ground Water Authority is constituted under the Environment (Protection) Act 1986 (UPSC 2022).
Atal Bhujal Yojana (2019, World Bank-aided) for community groundwater management in 7 States.
Most groundwater is used for irrigation, not drinking water (UPSC 2023 Statement-II trap).

nodes.title: Interlinking of Rivers — Debate, Benefits & Environmental Cost
prelimsNote: National Perspective Plan 1980: Himalayan (14 links) and Peninsular (16 links) components; NWDA prepares reports.
Ken–Betwa is the first link project approved (2021); Godavari–Krishna linked via Polavaram right canal (UPSC 2016).
Concerns: Panna Tiger Reserve submergence, forest loss, displacement, altered sediment flows.
Water is a State subject (Entry 17), with inter-state rivers under Union List Entry 56.

nodes.title: Water Management — Watershed Development & Rainwater Harvesting
prelimsNote: Watershed programmes conserve soil and water, recharge aquifers, raise productivity (UPSC 2014).
Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the Rain campaign; Mission Amrit Sarovar (2022): 75 water bodies per district.
Drip irrigation saves water and fertiliser, reduces weeds and salinity (UPSC 2016); fertigation improves nutrient efficiency (UPSC 2020).
Traditional systems: Dholavira reservoirs (UPSC 2021), johads, kuhls, zabo.

nodes.title: Deforestation — Causes, REDD+ & Compensatory Afforestation Fund
prelimsNote: REDD+ = reducing emissions from deforestation and forest degradation + conservation, sustainable management, enhancement of carbon stocks (UPSC 2016).
CAMPA Act 2016: compensatory afforestation funds — 90% to States, 10% to the Centre; non-lapsable public accounts (UPSC 2019).
ISFR (FSI, biennial): India's forest + tree cover about 25% (as of ISFR 2023).
Forest (Conservation) Amendment Act 2023 renamed the 1980 Act as Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam.

nodes.title: Forest Rights Act — Tribal Rights & Conflicts
prelimsNote: Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act 2006; nodal ministry: Tribal Affairs (UPSC 2021).
Gram Sabha initiates the process of determining individual and community forest rights (UPSC 2013).
Critical Wildlife Habitats under FRA can be declared inviolate only after due process (UPSC 2018).
Community Forest Resource rights let Gram Sabhas manage and protect forests.

nodes.title: Mining & Environment — Forest Clearance, Go/No-Go & Displacement
prelimsNote: Go/No-Go (2009–10) classified coal blocks in dense forests as 'no-go' — later diluted.
District Mineral Foundations (MMDR Amendment 2015) fund welfare in mining-affected areas (UPSC 2016).
Environmental clearance under EIA Notification 2006; forest clearance under the Forest Conservation law.
Coal ash and fly ash disposal pollutes air and water; fly ash is used in bricks and cement (UPSC 2015).

nodes.title: Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) — Process, Reforms & Controversies
prelimsNote: EIA notification first issued in 1994, revised in 2006 under the EP Act 1986.
Stages: screening, scoping, public consultation, appraisal; Category A projects appraised by the Centre, B by States (SEIAA).
Draft EIA Notification 2020 drew criticism for post-facto clearances.
Never directly asked in UPSC Prelims so far — a likely gap area.

nodes.title: Pollution Control Boards — Functioning, Challenges & Reforms
prelimsNote: CPCB constituted under the Water Act 1974; also given powers under the Air Act 1981.
SPCBs issue consent to establish/operate; CPCB coordinates and sets standards.
NGT can hear appeals against SPCB orders; CPCB is not a judicial body (UPSC 2018).
Never asked in detail in Prelims — the Air and Water Acts are classic gap areas.

nodes.title: National Green Tribunal (NGT) — Jurisdiction, Orders & Implementation
prelimsNote: NGT Act 2010 — rooted in Art 21; principal bench New Delhi; chairperson a retired SC judge or HC Chief Justice.
Hears civil cases under 7 laws (Water, Water Cess, Forest Conservation, Air, EP Act, Public Liability Insurance, Biological Diversity) — NOT the Wildlife Protection Act, Indian Forest Act or FRA.
Disposal within 6 months of filing (endeavour); appeals to the Supreme Court within 90 days.
NGT is a quasi-judicial tribunal (NGT Act 2010); CPCB is a statutory pollution regulator (Water Act 1974) — UPSC 2018 tested their differences.
Follows natural justice and the polluter-pays, precautionary and sustainable-development principles.

nodes.title: Environmental Laws — EPA, Wildlife Protection Act, Forest Conservation Act
prelimsNote: EP Act 1986 enacted under Art 253 after the Bhopal gas tragedy — umbrella law; GEAC and CGWA are constituted under it (UPSC 2015, 2022).
WPA 1972 amended 2022: schedules reduced to four — I (highest protection), II (lesser), III (protected plants), IV (CITES-listed specimens); vermin schedule removed.
Wild animals are government property; protected animals get equal protection inside and outside PAs (UPSC 2022).
Hunting of Schedule I animals is barred except in specified circumstances (UPSC 2017).
Forest (Conservation) Act 1980 requires Central approval for diversion of forest land; amended 2023.

nodes.title: Sustainable Development — Goals, Principles & India's Record
prelimsNote: Brundtland Report (1987): meeting present needs without compromising future generations.
Agenda 21 (Rio 1992) — non-binding action plan (UPSC 2016); Rio+20 (2012) launched the SDG process (UPSC 2015).
17 SDGs adopted in 2015 for 2030; NITI Aayog's SDG India Index tracks States (UPSC 2016).
Principles: polluter pays, precautionary, intergenerational equity, public trust doctrine.

nodes.title: Green Economy & Circular Economy
prelimsNote: UNEP's PAGE (Partnership for Action on Green Economy) helps countries transition (UPSC 2018).
TEEB (The Economics of Ecosystems and Biodiversity) values nature's services (UPSC 2016).
Circular economy: reduce, reuse, recycle; EPR across plastics, e-waste, batteries, tyres.
Greenwashing = falsely presenting products as eco-friendly (UPSC 2022).

nodes.title: Traditional Ecological Knowledge & Environment Ethics
prelimsNote: Sacred groves (orans, devrais, kavus) conserve biodiversity through community belief.
Bishnoi movement (1730, Khejarli) and Chipko (1973) are classic conservation movements.
GIAHS (FAO) recognises Koraput, Kuttanad and Saffron heritage of Kashmir (UPSC 2016).
Joint Forest Management (1990) involves village communities in protecting and regenerating forests.

newNodesToCreate.title: Ecological Interactions, Niche, Ecotone & Succession
prelimsNote: Niche = functional role and requirements of a species; habitat = where it lives (UPSC 2013).
Interactions: mutualism (lichens, mycorrhiza), commensalism (cattle egret–cattle — UPSC 2014), parasitism, predation, amensalism.
Ants that farm fungi (UPSC 2022); some species of pollinators decline → plant reproduction affected (butterflies — UPSC 2017).
Ecotone: transition zone with edge effect (more species); grasslands may not turn into forests because of water limits and fire (UPSC 2013).
Succession: lichens and mosses are pioneers on bare rock (UPSC 2021) → seral stages → climax community.

newNodesToCreate.title: Adaptations, Animal Behaviour & Microorganisms
prelimsNote: Hibernation is seen in bats, bears and rodents (UPSC 2014); some animals roll into balls for defence (pangolin, hedgehog — UPSC 2021).
Honeybees perform the waggle dance to signal food direction and distance (UPSC 2023); orangutans make tools from sticks (UPSC 2023).
Some turtles, fish and marine mammals (dugongs, manatees) are herbivores; some snakes are viviparous (UPSC 2019).
Extremophiles grow above boiling point, below freezing and below pH 3 (UPSC 2023); some mushrooms are medicinal, psychoactive, insecticidal and bioluminescent (UPSC 2023).
Desert plants reduce water loss through thick cuticles, tiny or no leaves, thorns (UPSC 2018).

newNodesToCreate.title: Indian Fauna & Flora — Species Identification, Habitat & IUCN Status
prelimsNote: UPSC's most-repeated Environment concept (tested in 10 separate papers): match a species to its habitat/range.
Range traps: Lion-tailed macaque — Western Ghats only; Indian wild ass — Rann of Kutch; Great Indian Hornbill — NE and Western Ghats; Musk deer — Himalaya (UPSC 2011, 2013, 2016, 2020).
Nocturnal: lion-tailed macaque is diurnal; Malabar civet and sambar are nocturnal/crepuscular (UPSC 2023); marsupials are not native to India (UPSC 2023).
Critically Endangered in India: Great Indian Bustard, Gharial, Bengal Florican, Jerdon's Courser, White-backed vulture (diclofenac decline — UPSC 2012).
Plants: Himalayan nettle (fibre — UPSC 2019), Gucchi (morel fungus — UPSC 2022), red sanders (endemic, Endangered — UPSC 2016).

newNodesToCreate.title: Protected Areas of India — Location, Rivers & Special Features
prelimsNote: Location questions recur almost every year (9 separate papers): State, river or region of a protected area.
Keibul Lamjao (Manipur) is the only floating national park (phumdis on Loktak — UPSC 2015); Namdapha has the widest altitudinal range (UPSC 2015).
Desert National Park spans Jaisalmer and Barmer and is a Great Indian Bustard habitat (UPSC 2020); Pakhui is in Arunachal (UPSC 2018).
Sathyamangalam links Eastern and Western Ghats (UPSC 2017); Cauvery-basin PAs: Nagarhole, Sathyamangalam, Wayanad (UPSC 2020).
Community Reserves are declared by the State Government on community/private land; hunting is not allowed (UPSC 2023).

newNodesToCreate.title: Invasive Alien Species & Species Recovery Programmes
prelimsNote: Invasive in India: Lantana camara, Prosopis juliflora, water hyacinth (Eichhornia), Parthenium (Prosopis juliflora — UPSC 2018).
IUCN's Invasive Species Specialist Group develops the Global Invasive Species Database (UPSC 2023).
Kunming–Montreal GBF targets a 50% cut in introduction rates of invasive species by 2030.
Recovery: Cheetah reintroduction at Kuno (2022); lions proposed for Kuno Palpur (UPSC 2017); GIB captive breeding.

newNodesToCreate.title: Hazardous Chemicals, Heavy Metals, Biomagnification & Fly Ash
prelimsNote: One of the most-repeated Environment concepts (8 papers): source ↔ chemical ↔ harm.
Mercury: gold mining and coal plants are sources; no known safe exposure level (UPSC 2023); lead from batteries, paints, petrol (UPSC 2012).
BPA in polycarbonate (endocrine disruptor), triclosan in toiletries, brominated flame retardants, benzene (UPSC 2014, 2020, 2021).
Biomagnification: concentration of persistent toxins (DDT, mercury) rises up the food chain.
Fly ash contains silica, alumina, iron oxides; used in bricks and cement (UPSC 2015); steel slag reused in roads (UPSC 2020).

newNodesToCreate.title: Greenhouse Gases, Ozone Depletion & Geo-engineering
prelimsNote: GWP (100-year): CO₂ = 1, methane ~28, N₂O ~265, HFCs and SF₆ thousands; water vapour is the most abundant GHG.
Oceans absorb CO₂ and acidify (UPSC 2011); phytoplankton act as a carbon sink (UPSC 2012).
Carbon capture options discussed (UPSC 2023): enhanced rock weathering (crushed basalt on farmland), ocean alkalinity enhancement (adding lime), CO₂ injection into abandoned mines.
Geo-engineering (UPSC 2019): stratospheric aerosol injection, cirrus cloud thinning, ocean iron fertilisation.
Blue carbon = carbon captured by oceans and coastal ecosystems (mangroves, seagrass, salt marshes) — UPSC 2021.

newNodesToCreate.title: Climate Finance & Forest-Carbon Mechanisms — GCF, GEF, REDD+, FCPF
prelimsNote: Green Climate Fund (2010) — mitigation and adaptation in developing countries, HQ South Korea (UPSC 2015).
GEF (1991) is the financial mechanism for UNFCCC, CBD, UNCCD, Stockholm and Minamata conventions (UPSC 2014).
World Bank's BioCarbon Fund (UPSC 2015) and Forest Carbon Partnership Facility (FCPF, supports REDD+ — UPSC 2015).
UN-REDD Programme (FAO, UNDP, UNEP) — REDD+ benefits include biodiversity and livelihoods (UPSC 2016).
Adaptation Fund (Kyoto) financed from a share of CDM proceeds.

newNodesToCreate.title: Global Climate & Environment Initiatives — Alliances, Coalitions & Trackers
prelimsNote: UPSC's favourite 'who runs it' area (7+ papers): Climate and Clean Air Coalition (UNEP-hosted, short-lived climate pollutants — UPSC 2017); Global Climate Change Alliance (EU — UPSC 2017).
Climate Action Tracker: independent research consortium, not an IPCC or UNFCCC body (UPSC 2022); Climate Neutral Now (UNFCCC — UPSC 2018).
The Climate Group runs RE100/EP100; Under2 Coalition secretariat is the Climate Group, not the IEA (UPSC 2022).
New York Declaration on Forests (2014, non-binding — UPSC 2021); Common Carbon Metric (UNEP-SBCI, buildings — UPSC 2021).
Earth Hour by WWF (UPSC 2014); Arbor Day Foundation + FAO run Tree Cities of the World (UPSC 2021).

newNodesToCreate.title: Chemical & Waste Conventions — Basel, Rotterdam, Stockholm & Minamata
prelimsNote: Basel (1989): transboundary movement of hazardous wastes; Rotterdam (1998): Prior Informed Consent for hazardous chemicals/pesticides trade.
Stockholm (2001): eliminate Persistent Organic Pollutants (the 'dirty dozen' incl. DDT, aldrin); Minamata (2013): mercury — India ratified in 2018.
BRS conventions share a joint UNEP secretariat in Geneva.
Never directly asked in UPSC Prelims so far — a strong candidate for a future question.

newNodesToCreate.title: Biological Diversity Act, BMCs & Access and Benefit Sharing
prelimsNote: Biological Diversity Act 2002 (amended 2023) gives effect to the CBD; three-tier structure: NBA (Chennai), State Biodiversity Boards, Biodiversity Management Committees.
BMCs (local bodies) maintain People's Biodiversity Registers and can levy collection fees for access to bio-resources in their area (UPSC 2023).
BMCs are key to realising the Nagoya Protocol's access and benefit-sharing objectives (UPSC 2023).
Foreigners need NBA approval to access Indian bio-resources; 2023 amendment eased rules for AYUSH and Indian companies.

newNodesToCreate.title: Wildlife Protection Act 2022 & Wildlife Institutions — NTCA, WCCB, CZA, AWBI
prelimsNote: WPA amendment 2022: four schedules — I (highest), II, III (protected plants), IV (CITES specimens); the old Schedule VI (specified plants whose cultivation needs a licence — UPSC 2020) is now absorbed into the reorganised schedules.
Statutory bodies: NTCA (2006 amendment), WCCB (2006), Central Zoo Authority (1991), National Board for Wildlife (2002, chaired by PM).
Animal Welfare Board of India is statutory under the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act 1960 (UPSC 2014).
Trap: Schedule III covers protected PLANTS and Schedule IV covers CITES-listed specimens — not the other way round; vermin schedule (old Schedule V) was removed.
